tool.name: faToTwoBit
tool.description: : convert FASTA to the 2bit format a UCSC assembly hub serves
tool.command: ## ⛔ SOFT-MASKING IS CARRIED IN THE CASE, AND THE DEFAULT KEEPS IT. 2bit stores an explicit mask ## block list, so a lower-cased FASTA converts to a MASKED 2bit and `-noMask` silently discards ## that. For this stack the difference is not cosmetic: lastz seeds only on uppercase, so a hub ## built from a `-noMask` 2bit shows masked repeats the aligner never looked at. ## ⛔ EVERY FLAG LIVES IN truevalue, AND THAT IS NOT STYLE. Galaxy renders a boolean as the ## STRING "true" or "false", and "false" is truthy in Python -- so `#if $options.noMask` was ## ALWAYS true and this tool would have passed -noMask on every run, silently discarding the ## soft-mask from every genome it converted. The flag as the value cannot fail that way. faToTwoBit $options.noMask $options.long $options.stripVersion $options.ignoreDups #if str($options.namePrefix).strip() -namePrefix='$options.namePrefix' #end if #for $f in $input '$f' #end for '$output'

param.name: input
param.label: FASTA sequence(s)
param.help: More than one file is concatenated into a single 2bit, in the order given.

param.label: Discard soft-masking
param.help: ⛔ Lower-case is the mask. Leave this off unless you specifically want an unmasked 2bit.

param.label: 64-bit offsets
param.help: Required only for a genome over 4 Gb. Produces a 2bit older tools cannot read.

param.label: Strip the version suffix from GenBank accessions
param.help: CM123456.1 becomes CM123456. ⚠ The hub's chrom.sizes and every track must agree with this choice.

param.label: Keep only the first of a duplicated sequence name
param.help: Without it, a duplicate name is a fatal error — which is usually what you want.

param.name: namePrefix
param.label: Prefix every sequence name
param.help: Prepended verbatim, e.g. an assembly tag for a multi-genome hub.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Converts FASTA to UCSC's `2bit`_ format: two bits per base, with runs of ``N`` and the soft-mask stored as separate block lists rather than in the sequence. An assembly hub names one per genome in its ``genomes.txt`` ``twoBitPath`` stanza, and the Genome Browser reads ranges out of it directly.
**Masking**
Lower-case characters in the input become the 2bit's mask block list. ``-noMask`` throws that away.
.. warning:: Alignment tools in this stack seed only on uppercase, so a hub built from an unmasked 2bit displays repeats that the aligner never examined. Keep the default unless you know otherwise.
**Sequence names**
``-stripVersion`` and ``-namePrefix`` both rewrite names. Whatever you choose, the hub's ``chrom.sizes``, every BED fed to ``bedToBigBed``, and the ``defaultPos`` in ``genomes.txt`` must use the same names, or tracks silently fail to display.
.. _2bit: https://genome.ucsc.edu/FAQ/FAQformat.html#format7
